names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 28 mai, «Sfânta Muceniță Eliconida».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 28 Μαΐου, «Αγία Ελικωνίδα», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 28. мај ст. ст., „Света мученица Еликонида“ — Света is not a rank and мученица is the `martyr` this corpus puts in `types`; the bare personal name is what is left. **Measured**: `foldchk.py` returns `NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM` for «Еликонида», so this is the first folder to hold it and the corpus keeps no other woman of the name. **The body spells it once «Елконида**, without the и, in „уздиже Елконида руке своје“ — **that shorter spelling is not stored**: one `sr` form per folder, the fullest, and the heading’s form is the fuller and the one the entry uses everywhere else. It is named here so a later reader who meets «Елконида» knows which folder holds it. The Greek form, «Ελικωνίδα», and the Romanian «Eliconida» are the same name.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 28 mai — «Sfânta Muceniță Eliconida»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 28ης Μαΐου — «Αγία Ελικωνίδα»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 28 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing and the same day as the folder's Romanian row, and it is plainly the same woman: of Thessalonica, tried at Corinth, beheaded at the last. No hymn is printed.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 10.06.2026 (28. мај ст. ст.) — „Света мученица Еликонида“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry, on the same menologion 28/5 the Romanian and Greek rows already carry. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of the 23 to 28 May is. **The `[~]` mark fired on this line and was wrong**, as it is a hint and not a decision: „Света мученица“ reads to it like a feast word and she is a person. **A SECOND EMPEROR, AND IT IS REFUSED AS A SOURCE FOR A YEAR.** This folder holds `death` 238 to 244, „mid 3rd century“, off **saint.gr’s own stated interval** for the reign of Gordian III. **The Prologue says „У време Гордијана и Филипа“** — in the time of Gordian **and Philip** — which is a second reign the Greek page does not mention, and Philip reigned after Gordian. **Widening the folder’s `latest` past 244 to take Philip in would mean supplying Philip’s regnal years myself, because no book read for this folder states them**, and this corpus refuses a date derived from a reign and refuses an unbounded one. **So `dates` is untouched and the second emperor is recorded in the prose.** The 238 to 244 stands as saint.gr’s own numbers, not as a reading of a reign. **It is the author’s to widen if he wishes, off a source that states the years.** **THE TWO BOOKS REVERSE WHO DENOUNCED WHOM.** saint.gr has her **denounced as a Christian to the ruler Perinios**. **The Prologue has her denounce the idolaters**: „она пређе у Коринт где велегласно изобличи све оне који приношаху жртве идолима“, she went over to Corinth where she loudly rebuked all those who offered sacrifice to idols. **Neither account was altered and both stand in the life.** **And the torments are a different list in each.** saint.gr has molten lead and pitch under Perinios, then fire and wild beasts under **the proconsul Justin**, then the sword. **The Prologue has no lead, no pitch and no Justin**, and instead: that **she was thrown into fire, and much blood poured out of her body and quenched it, and she stayed alive**; that **she was thrown before lions and the lions did not touch her but fawned about her**; that **let into the temple to sacrifice she smashed the idols**; that **as she lay all wounded in prison the Lord Himself appeared to her with the archangels Michael and Gabriel, healed her wounds and comforted and strengthened her**; and that at the scaffold **she raised her hands and prayed, and a voice was heard from heaven, „Приђи, крећи, готов је за тебе и венац и престо!“** — come, set out, both the crown and the throne are ready for thee. **Only the beheading is in both.** **Асклепius IS NAMED HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE**: „Када је начелник Периније саветоваше да принесе жртву идолу Ескулапу“, and her answer „Чуј ме, ја сам слушкиња Христова, а ко је Ескулап, не знам. Чини што ти воља“ — hear me, I am a handmaid of Christ, and who Asclepius is I do not know; do as you please. saint.gr names no god. **Her Thessalonican birth and the move to Corinth are in both books and agree.** **NO ROW FOR THE ARCHANGELS, AND NOT BECAUSE THE TEST DID NOT FIRE.** The corpus keeps no folder for Michael or Gabriel the archangel — `ls saints | grep -iE 'archangel'` returns nothing, and the twenty-four Gabriels and the Michaels it does keep are men. **An archangel is not a saint with a folder in this corpus**, and the appearance of the Lord Himself is no more a `related` row than a dedication is. They are named in the prose. The ruler Perinios gains nothing by the coordinator’s third ruling, the martyrdom belonging to her and not to the persecutor. `martyr` is corroborated and **no type was added**: the entry calls her „Христова мученица“ and nothing else, and **`virgin` is NOT written although the closing image is „као невино и чисто јагње“** — an innocent and pure lamb is a figure for the sacrifice and not the rank Девица, which this heading does not print. `related` stays empty. No `locations`, although Thessalonica and Corinth are named in both books. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

death.note: saint.gr puts her reign and its years itself: «Η Αγία Ελικωνίδα έζησε στα χρόνια του βασιλιά Γορδιανού του Γ', στα μέσα του 3ου μ.Χ. αιώνα (238 - 244 μ.Χ.)». The bracket is the page's own; it gives no year for her death.
